7	+# Match information (intel)
8	+
9	+The pure rules behind §2's timed reveals, §3's rumors and journal, §5's final-island announcement and §11's comeback leads. `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/intel` has the config, the state, `stepIntel`, `targetedRumorAvailability` and `replayIntel`. `@pirate-sea-race/content/intel` has the constants and the zod validator `validateIntelRules`. The module doesn't import the ledger. It is integer data with no clocks and no `Math.random`, and time is the world tick (20 per second). `objectives-endgame` wires it into `MatchRoom`; nothing calls it yet.
10	+
11	+## Constants (`intelRules`)
12	+
13	+| Rule | Value |
14	+| --- | --- |
15	+| Sector grid | 3 × 3, named row by row from "North-West Reach" to "South-East Reach" |
16	+| Sighting delay | 600 ticks (30 s), equal to the carrier interval |
17	+| Carrier interval | 600 ticks (30 s) |
18	+| Sector reveal | 24,000 ticks (minute 20) after control start |
19	+| Carrier reveal | 33,600 ticks (minute 28) after control start |
20	+| Targeted rumor price | 25 gold (the caller charges it) |
21	+
22	+The validator refuses a zero interval, reveals out of order, a delay that differs from the interval, and names that are missing or repeated.
23	+
24	+## Sectors
25	+
26	+`sectorOfTile` cuts the map's columns and rows into three bands each by integer division (`floor(tile × 3 / width)`). Every tile is in exactly one sector, and bands differ by at most one tile. On the 224 × 208 slice sea, the columns start at tiles 0, 75 and 150 and the rows at 0, 70 and 139. `sectorOf(position)` is the sector of the position's tile. A position off the map counts in the nearest edge sector. The config computes all of this from the map size, so the same code serves the slice and the 12-island alpha.
27	+
28	+## Leads
29	+
30	+A rumor names a missing type and a target: an **island**, where a source of that type is still sealed, or a **sector**, where a recovery cache holds one. It never names a rubbing, a player or a position. The generator picks among the eligible targets with the seeded generator (`random.ts`), so the same seed gives the same rumor. It tries three tiers in order:
31	+
32	+1. the islands with a sealed source of the type;
33	+2. the sectors with a cached copy;
34	+3. a **carrier sighting**, and only when every copy of the type is carried by someone else.
35	+
36	+Targets already active in the player's journal are skipped, so a player is never given the same lead twice.
37	+
38	+Leads are made on four occasions:
39	+
40	+- a **start** rumor for each player at control start, or when a player is first seen after it;
41	+- a free **fresh** rumor for each type a player lost (§11);
42	+- a **targeted** rumor, bought on request;
43	+- a **replacement**, when a journal rumor goes stale.
44	+
45	+Losses and completions come from diffing each player's held types between ticks. A rubbing reserved in a duel still counts as held, so entering a duel is never a loss; only a settled theft is.
46	+
47	+**Journal rumors** (island or sector) are the only leads tracked:
48	+
49	+- A rumor goes **stale** when its target no longer holds its type: the source was collected or the cache claimed by someone else. The player gets `rumor-stale` with the tick and then a replacement.
50	+- A rumor whose type the holder obtains, by any means, is **resolved** quietly. It gets no replacement.
51	+
52	+**Carrier sightings** are one-shot messages, never tracked, so they can never go stale and can't be used to follow a carrier. At every carrier boundary (control start plus a multiple of 30 s, counted when crossed), the state takes one snapshot of the carried copies: the sector, the type and the internal holder of each. It keeps the latest two. A sighting reads the **older** of the two, so it is 30–60 s old and never the current position. It also skips the requester's own former entries.
53	+
54	+A `carrier-sighting` message may list several types: one entry per type (the type, the trigger's reason and a sector), all from the same older snapshot. Before minute 28, a player gets at most **one sighting message per snapshot**. A targeted request that hits this cap is answered `capped`.
55	+
56	+A free trigger (start, fresh or replacement) that hits the cap, or that finds no usable snapshot entry yet, is **deferred**. A player has at most **one pending** sighting message, which holds the **set** of pending types; a new capped free trigger adds its type to that set. At the next boundary the pending message goes out with every pending type that is still eligible, so a player who lost two types learns about both at once. A pending type that now has a source or cache gets a journal rumor instead, one the player obtained is dropped, and one with no copy left sends `no-lead`. A type whose previous snapshot shows no other carrier yet stays pending for the boundary after. A free trigger with nothing at all to point at sends `no-lead`.
57	+
58	+**Targeted requests** are `{ requestId, playerId, type }`, and each gets exactly one outcome, whatever the order of the batch:
59	+
60	+- `rumor` or `sighting`: something was delivered. Charge the 25 gold only for these two.
61	+- `capped`: the player already got a sighting in this snapshot.
62	+- `none`: nothing to sell. The player holds the type, or the player is unknown, or it is before control start, or no untracked target exists.
63	+- `duplicate`: the request id was seen before. The step answers it without changing the state or drawing from the generator.
64	+
65	+`targetedRumorAvailability(config, state, view, playerId, type)` gives the same answer without drawing, so the UI can show whether buying would yield anything.
66	+
67	+## Reveals (§2, §5)
68	+
69	+All reveals fire when their tick is crossed since the last processed tick, so a skipped tick never loses one. Nothing is sent before control start.
70	+
71	+- **First full set:** the first player to hold every type of the preset triggers `final-sector` (the final island's sector) to everyone. Each holder of a full set gets `final-route` with the exact point: the first completer, later completers, and anyone who restores a broken set (with `restored: true`). A player who loses a type gets `final-route-inactive`.
72	+- **Minute 20:** `sector-reveal` to everyone, listing the sectors with sealed sources and the sectors with caches.
73	+- **Minute 28, then every 30 s:** `carrier-report` to everyone, listing the (sector, type) pairs of the newest snapshot. Skipping several beats sends one report.
74	+- **Minute 35** belongs to the claim code.
75	+
76	+## Messages and hidden information (§16)
77	+
78	+`stepIntel(config, state, view, requests) → { state, messages, outcomes }` never writes into its input. Each message is `{ to, body }`, where `to` is `{ kind: "player", playerId }`, `{ kind: "players", playerIds }` or `{ kind: "everyone" }`. Broadcasts are `final-sector`, `sector-reveal` and `carrier-report`; every other kind goes to one player.
79	+
80	+Bodies carry sectors, island indexes and names, types, ticks and journal entry numbers. They never carry a player id, a rubbing id, or a source's, cache's or ship's position. The one exact position ever sent is the final island's, in a `final-route` to a full-set holder. The property tests check every message of every run against these rules:
81	+
82	+- five seeded runs with compressed reveal times;
83	+- one slice run with the real constants for 36,660 ticks;
84	+- one alpha run with the real constants that skips ticks.
85	+
86	+The same runs also check, after every step, that each player has at most one pending sighting message and that every deferred type goes out at the first boundary after it was capped (or is dropped only when the checker finds it ineligible, or kept only when the previous snapshot shows no other carrier of it). Every rumor is checked against the preference: a cache lead only when no sealed source of the type is left outside the player's journal, a carrier sighting only when no source or cache of the type exists. Their `EXERCISED` check asserts that every message kind, outcome and lead path occurred, including a deferred delivery and a message with several types.
87	+
88	+## Building the world view from the ledger
89	+
90	+On each processed tick, the caller passes `{ tick, players, rubbings }`:
91	+
92	+- **`players`:** each player still in the match (`status` not `left`), with the ship's position in sub-units.
93	+- **`rubbings`:** each ledger rubbing with its `type` and its `location` resolved to a place:
94	+  - `source` becomes `{ kind: "source", island, x, y }` from its `LedgerSource`;
95	+  - `cache` becomes `{ kind: "cache", x, y }` from its `LedgerCache`;
96	+  - `player` becomes `{ kind: "carried", playerId }`;
97	+  - `duel` becomes `{ kind: "duel", playerId }`.
98	+
99	+Held types and claimed-out islands (islands with no sealed source left) follow from the rubbings, so they can't disagree with them. The ledger's sticky `freshRumors` flag isn't read. The config comes from `createIntelConfig({ preset, finalIsland, controlStartTick, map })`. The state comes from `createIntelState(config, seed)`, which starts before control start.
100	+
101	+## Decisions taken here
102	+
103	+- Held types and claimed-out islands are derived from the view's rubbings rather than passed separately.
104	+- A pending sighting is one message per player holding a set of types, so two types that need a sighting at once are delivered together at the next boundary, not one interval apart, and the cap stays one sighting message per 30 s before minute 28.
105	+- A free trigger that finds every copy carried but no snapshot entry to read yet waits like a capped one.
106	+- Targeted requests in one batch are handled in request-id order, so the order they are listed in never changes the result.

+# Match information (intel)
+
+The pure rules behind §2's timed reveals, §3's rumors and journal, §5's final-island announcement and §11's comeback leads. `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/intel` has the config, the state, `stepIntel`, `targetedRumorAvailability` and `replayIntel`. `@pirate-sea-race/content/intel` has the constants and the zod validator `validateIntelRules`. The module doesn't import the ledger. It is integer data with no clocks and no `Math.random`, and time is the world tick (20 per second). `objectives-endgame` wires it into `MatchRoom`; nothing calls it yet.
+
+## Constants (`intelRules`)
+
+| Rule | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| Sector grid | 3 × 3, named row by row from "North-West Reach" to "South-East Reach" |
+| Sighting delay | 600 ticks (30 s), equal to the carrier interval |
+| Carrier interval | 600 ticks (30 s) |
+| Sector reveal | 24,000 ticks (minute 20) after control start |
+| Carrier reveal | 33,600 ticks (minute 28) after control start |
+| Targeted rumor price | 25 gold (the caller charges it) |
+
+The validator refuses a zero interval, reveals out of order, a delay that differs from the interval, and names that are missing or repeated.
+
+## Sectors
+
+`sectorOfTile` cuts the map's columns and rows into three bands each by integer division (`floor(tile × 3 / width)`). Every tile is in exactly one sector, and bands differ by at most one tile. On the 224 × 208 slice sea, the columns start at tiles 0, 75 and 150 and the rows at 0, 70 and 139. `sectorOf(position)` is the sector of the position's tile. A position off the map counts in the nearest edge sector. The config computes all of this from the map size, so the same code serves the slice and the 12-island alpha.
+
+## Leads
+
+A rumor names a missing type and a target: an **island**, where a source of that type is still sealed, or a **sector**, where a recovery cache holds one. It never names a rubbing, a player or a position. The generator picks among the eligible targets with the seeded generator (`random.ts`), so the same seed gives the same rumor. It tries three tiers in order:
+
+1. the islands with a sealed source of the type;
+2. the sectors with a cached copy;
+3. a **carrier sighting**, and only when every copy of the type is carried by someone else.
+
+Targets already active in the player's journal are skipped, so a player is never given the same lead twice.
+
+Leads are made on four occasions:
+
+- a **start** rumor for each player at control start, or when a player is first seen after it;
+- a free **fresh** rumor for each type a player lost (§11);
+- a **targeted** rumor, bought on request;
+- a **replacement**, when a journal rumor goes stale.
+
+Losses and completions come from diffing each player's held types between ticks. A rubbing reserved in a duel still counts as held, so entering a duel is never a loss; only a settled theft is.
+
+**Journal rumors** (island or sector) are the only leads tracked:
+
+- A rumor goes **stale** when its target no longer holds its type: the source was collected or the cache claimed by someone else. The player gets `rumor-stale` with the tick and then a replacement.
+- A rumor whose type the holder obtains, by any means, is **resolved** quietly. It gets no replacement.
+
+**Carrier sightings** are one-shot messages, never tracked, so they can never go stale and can't be used to follow a carrier. At every carrier boundary (control start plus a multiple of 30 s, counted when crossed), the state takes one snapshot of the carried copies: the sector, the type and the internal holder of each. It keeps the latest two. A sighting reads the **older** of the two, so it is 30–60 s old and never the current position. It also skips the requester's own former entries.
+
+A `carrier-sighting` message may list several types: one entry per type (the type, the trigger's reason and a sector), all from the same older snapshot. Before minute 28, a player gets at most **one sighting message per snapshot**. A targeted request that hits this cap is answered `capped`.
+
+A free trigger (start, fresh or replacement) that hits the cap, or that finds no usable snapshot entry yet, is **deferred**. A player has at most **one pending** sighting message, which holds the **set** of pending types; a new capped free trigger adds its type to that set. At the next boundary the pending message goes out with every pending type that is still eligible, so a player who lost two types learns about both at once. A pending type that now has a source or cache gets a journal rumor instead, one the player obtained is dropped, and one with no copy left sends `no-lead`. A type whose previous snapshot shows no other carrier yet stays pending for the boundary after. A free trigger with nothing at all to point at sends `no-lead`.
+
+**Targeted requests** are `{ requestId, playerId, type }`, and each gets exactly one outcome, whatever the order of the batch:
+
+- `rumor` or `sighting`: something was delivered. Charge the 25 gold only for these two.
+- `capped`: the player already got a sighting in this snapshot.
+- `none`: nothing to sell. The player holds the type, or the player is unknown, or it is before control start, or no untracked target exists.
+- `duplicate`: the request id was seen before. The step answers it without changing the state or drawing from the generator.
+
+`targetedRumorAvailability(config, state, view, playerId, type)` gives the same answer without drawing, so the UI can show whether buying would yield anything.
+
+## Reveals (§2, §5)
+
+All reveals fire when their tick is crossed since the last processed tick, so a skipped tick never loses one. Nothing is sent before control start.
+
+- **First full set:** the first player to hold every type of the preset triggers `final-sector` (the final island's sector) to everyone. Each holder of a full set gets `final-route` with the exact point: the first completer, later completers, and anyone who restores a broken set (with `restored: true`). A player who loses a type gets `final-route-inactive`.
+- **Minute 20:** `sector-reveal` to everyone, listing the sectors with sealed sources and the sectors with caches.
+- **Minute 28, then every 30 s:** `carrier-report` to everyone, listing the (sector, type) pairs of the newest snapshot. Skipping several beats sends one report.
+- **Minute 35** belongs to the claim code.
+
+## Messages and hidden information (§16)
+
+`stepIntel(config, state, view, requests) → { state, messages, outcomes }` never writes into its input. Each message is `{ to, body }`, where `to` is `{ kind: "player", playerId }`, `{ kind: "players", playerIds }` or `{ kind: "everyone" }`. Broadcasts are `final-sector`, `sector-reveal` and `carrier-report`; every other kind goes to one player.
+
+Bodies carry sectors, island indexes and names, types, ticks and journal entry numbers. They never carry a player id, a rubbing id, or a source's, cache's or ship's position. The one exact position ever sent is the final island's, in a `final-route` to a full-set holder. The property tests check every message of every run against these rules:
+
+- five seeded runs with compressed reveal times;
+- one slice run with the real constants for 36,660 ticks;
+- one alpha run with the real constants that skips ticks.
+
+The same runs also check, after every step, that each player has at most one pending sighting message and that every deferred type goes out at the first boundary after it was capped (or is dropped only when the checker finds it ineligible, or kept only when the previous snapshot shows no other carrier of it). Every rumor is checked against the preference: a cache lead only when no sealed source of the type is left outside the player's journal, a carrier sighting only when no source or cache of the type exists. Their `EXERCISED` check asserts that every message kind, outcome and lead path occurred, including a deferred delivery and a message with several types.
+
+## Building the world view from the ledger
+
+On each processed tick, the caller passes `{ tick, players, rubbings }`:
+
+- **`players`:** each player still in the match (`status` not `left`), with the ship's position in sub-units.
+- **`rubbings`:** each ledger rubbing with its `type` and its `location` resolved to a place:
+  - `source` becomes `{ kind: "source", island, x, y }` from its `LedgerSource`;
+  - `cache` becomes `{ kind: "cache", x, y }` from its `LedgerCache`;
+  - `player` becomes `{ kind: "carried", playerId }`;
+  - `duel` becomes `{ kind: "duel", playerId }`.
+
+Held types and claimed-out islands (islands with no sealed source left) follow from the rubbings, so they can't disagree with them. The ledger's sticky `freshRumors` flag isn't read. The config comes from `createIntelConfig({ preset, finalIsland, controlStartTick, map })`. The state comes from `createIntelState(config, seed)`, which starts before control start.
+
+## Decisions taken here
+
+- Held types and claimed-out islands are derived from the view's rubbings rather than passed separately.
+- A pending sighting is one message per player holding a set of types, so two types that need a sighting at once are delivered together at the next boundary, not one interval apart, and the cap stays one sighting message per 30 s before minute 28.
+- A free trigger that finds every copy carried but no snapshot entry to read yet waits like a capped one.
+- Targeted requests in one batch are handled in request-id order, so the order they are listed in never changes the result.

+import { z } from "zod";
+import { formatIssues, type ValidationResult } from "../rules.js";
+import { WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND } from "../sailing.js";
+
+/** The sea is split into a grid of named sectors this many columns wide and rows high (§2's "sectors"). */
+export const SECTOR_COLUMNS = 3;
+export const SECTOR_ROWS = 3;
+
+/** The nine sector names, row by row from the north-west corner. */
+export const SECTOR_NAMES = [
+  "North-West Reach",
+  "Northern Waters",
+  "North-East Reach",
+  "Western Waters",
+  "Central Waters",
+  "Eastern Waters",
+  "South-West Reach",
+  "Southern Waters",
+  "South-East Reach",
+] as const;
+
+/**
+ * §11: a carrier sighting is coarse and delayed. It reads the carrier snapshot taken one interval before the latest,
+ * so it is at least this old (and less than twice this old), never the current location.
+ */
+export const CARRIER_SIGHTING_DELAY_SECONDS = 30;
+/** §2: from minute 28 the carriers' sectors are published every 30 seconds; the carrier snapshots keep the same beat. */
+export const CARRIER_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 30;
+/** §2: at minute 20 the sectors holding unclaimed rubbings and abandoned caches are revealed. */
+export const SECTOR_REVEAL_MINUTE = 20;
+/** §2: from minute 28 the carriers' approximate sectors are published. */
+export const CARRIER_REVEAL_MINUTE = 28;
+/** §11: what the caller charges for a targeted rumor that delivers something. */
+export const TARGETED_RUMOR_GOLD = 25;
+
+/** The information rules (§2, §3, §11) in world ticks (20 a second), counted from the start of player control. */
+export const intelRulesSchema = z
+  .strictObject({
+    sectorColumns: z.int().positive(),
+    sectorRows: z.int().positive(),
+    /** Row by row from the north-west; one unique, non-empty name per sector. */
+    sectorNames: z.array(z.string().min(1)),
+    /** How old a carrier sighting is at least; it must equal the carrier interval, since sightings read the previous snapshot. */
+    sightingDelayTicks: z.int().positive(),
+    /** The beat of the carrier snapshots, of the sighting cap and, from the carrier reveal on, of the carrier broadcasts. */
+    carrierIntervalTicks: z.int().positive(),
+    /** Ticks from control start to the reveal of the sectors holding unclaimed rubbings and caches. */
+    sectorRevealTicks: z.int().positive(),
+    /** Ticks from control start to the first carrier broadcast. */
+    carrierRevealTicks: z.int().positive(),
+    targetedRumorGold: z.int().nonnegative(),
+  })
+  .superRefine((rules, ctx) => {
+    if (rules.sectorNames.length !== rules.sectorColumns * rules.sectorRows) {
+      ctx.addIssue({
+        code: "custom",
+        path: ["sectorNames"],
+        message: `${rules.sectorNames.length} names for a ${rules.sectorColumns} × ${rules.sectorRows} grid`,
+      });
+    }
+    if (new Set(rules.sectorNames).size !== rules.sectorNames.length) {
+      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["sectorNames"], message: "sector names must be unique" });
+    }
+    if (rules.sightingDelayTicks !== rules.carrierIntervalTicks) {
+      ctx.addIssue({
+        code: "custom",
+        path: ["sightingDelayTicks"],
+        message: `the sighting delay (${rules.sightingDelayTicks} ticks) must equal the carrier interval (${rules.carrierIntervalTicks} ticks)`,
+      });
+    }
+    if (rules.sectorRevealTicks >= rules.carrierRevealTicks) {
+      ctx.addIssue({
+        code: "custom",
+        path: ["carrierRevealTicks"],
+        message: `the carrier reveal (${rules.carrierRevealTicks} ticks) must come after the sector reveal (${rules.sectorRevealTicks} ticks)`,
+      });
+    }
+  });
+
+export type IntelRules = z.infer<typeof intelRulesSchema>;
+
+export const intelRules: IntelRules = {
+  sectorColumns: SECTOR_COLUMNS,
+  sectorRows: SECTOR_ROWS,
+  sectorNames: [...SECTOR_NAMES],
+  sightingDelayTicks: CARRIER_SIGHTING_DELAY_SECONDS * WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND,
+  carrierIntervalTicks: CARRIER_INTERVAL_SECONDS * WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND,
+  sectorRevealTicks: SECTOR_REVEAL_MINUTE * 60 * WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND,
+  carrierRevealTicks: CARRIER_REVEAL_MINUTE * 60 * WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND,
+  targetedRumorGold: TARGETED_RUMOR_GOLD,
+};
+
+export function validateIntelRules(candidate: unknown): ValidationResult<IntelRules> {
+  const parsed = intelRulesSchema.safeParse(candidate);
+  return parsed.success ? { ok: true, value: parsed.data } : { ok: false, issues: formatIssues(parsed.error) };
+}

+import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
+import {
+  createIntelConfig,
+  createIntelState,
+  hashState,
+  intelRules,
+  replayIntel,
+  stepIntel,
+  targetedRumorAvailability,
+  type IntelConfig,
+  type IntelMessage,
+  type IntelMessageBody,
+  type IntelPoint,
+  type IntelRubbing,
+  type IntelState,
+  type IntelStepResult,
+  type IntelWorldView,
+  type RubbingType,
+  type TargetedRumorRequest,
+} from "./index.js";
+
+const T = 256;
+const tile = (x: number, y: number): IntelPoint => ({ x: x * T + 128, y: y * T + 128 });
+/** A 30 × 30 test sea: sector bands are tiles 0–9, 10–19 and 20–29. Islands sit in the four corner sectors. */
+const MAP = {
+  widthTiles: 30,
+  heightTiles: 30,
+  subUnitsPerTile: T,
+  islands: [{ name: "Palm Key" }, { name: "Ash Isle" }, { name: "Mist Rock" }, { name: "Old Ruin" }],
+};
+const ISLAND_AT = [tile(4, 4), tile(25, 4), tile(4, 25), tile(25, 25)];
+const ISLAND_SECTOR = [0, 2, 6, 8];
+/** A point in each of the nine sectors. */
+const S = [tile(2, 2), tile(15, 2), tile(27, 2), tile(2, 15), tile(15, 15), tile(27, 15), tile(2, 27), tile(15, 27), tile(27, 27)] as const;
+const FINAL = { x: 15 * T + 7, y: 16 * T + 3 };
+const START = 100;
+
+/** Real reveal times and a 100-tick (5 s) carrier interval, so carrier scenarios stay short. */
+const quick = createIntelConfig({
+  preset: "slice",
+  finalIsland: FINAL,
+  controlStartTick: START,
+  map: MAP,
+  rules: { ...intelRules, carrierIntervalTicks: 100, sightingDelayTicks: 100, sectorRevealTicks: 1_000, carrierRevealTicks: 2_000 },
+});
+const real = createIntelConfig({ preset: "slice", finalIsland: FINAL, controlStartTick: START, map: MAP });
+/** The quick timings with the alpha's four types (sun, moon, tide, storm), so several types can wait at once. */
+const quickAlpha = createIntelConfig({
+  preset: "alpha",
+  finalIsland: FINAL,
+  controlStartTick: START,
+  map: MAP,
+  rules: { ...intelRules, carrierIntervalTicks: 100, sightingDelayTicks: 100, sectorRevealTicks: 1_000, carrierRevealTicks: 2_000 },
+});
+
+const typeOf = (id: string) => id.slice(0, id.indexOf("-")) as RubbingType;
+const source = (id: string, island: number): IntelRubbing => ({ id, type: typeOf(id), place: { kind: "source", island, ...ISLAND_AT[island]! } });
+const cached = (id: string, at: IntelPoint): IntelRubbing => ({ id, type: typeOf(id), place: { kind: "cache", ...at } });
+const carried = (id: string, playerId: string): IntelRubbing => ({ id, type: typeOf(id), place: { kind: "carried", playerId } });
+const reserved = (id: string, playerId: string): IntelRubbing => ({ id, type: typeOf(id), place: { kind: "duel", playerId } });
+
+interface World {
+  readonly players: Readonly<Record<string, IntelPoint>>;
+  readonly rubbings: readonly IntelRubbing[];
+}
+
+/** Recursively frozen, so a step that mutated its input would throw. */
+function deepFreeze<T>(value: T): T {
+  if (typeof value === "object" && value !== null && !Object.isFrozen(value)) {
+    Object.freeze(value);
+    for (const child of Object.values(value)) deepFreeze(child);
+  }
+  return value;
+}
+
+function viewOf(tick: number, world: World): IntelWorldView {
+  return { tick, players: Object.entries(world.players).map(([id, at]) => ({ id, ...at })), rubbings: world.rubbings };
+}
+
+/** Steps with frozen input and state, checking neither changes. */
+class Run {
+  state: IntelState;
+  constructor(
+    readonly config: IntelConfig,
+    seed = 1,
+  ) {
+    this.state = createIntelState(config, seed);
+  }
+
+  step(tick: number, world: World, requests: TargetedRumorRequest[] = []): IntelStepResult {
+    const view = deepFreeze(viewOf(tick, world));
+    const before = hashState(deepFreeze(this.state));
+    const stepped = stepIntel(this.config, this.state, view, deepFreeze(requests));
+    expect(hashState(this.state)).toBe(before);
+    this.state = stepped.state;
+    return stepped;
+  }
+
+  available(tick: number, world: World, playerId: string, type: RubbingType) {
+    return targetedRumorAvailability(this.config, this.state, viewOf(tick, world), playerId, type);
+  }
+}
+
+function to(result: IntelStepResult, playerId: string): IntelMessageBody[] {
+  return result.messages.filter((message) => message.to.kind === "player" && message.to.playerId === playerId).map((message) => message.body);
+}
+
+function everyone(result: IntelStepResult): IntelMessageBody[] {
+  return result.messages.filter((message) => message.to.kind === "everyone").map((message) => message.body);
+}

- **When it happens:**

  - a theft on the same tick another rumor goes stale;
  - two journal rumors emptied on one tick.
